heading: Split features form nested, geometrically close families that mirror a hierarchy of concepts
definition: split features form nested, geometrically close families that mirror a hierarchy of concepts in the model's representation.
summary: Nested families formed by splitting across dictionary sizes appear only in qualitative GPT-2 small examples, from posts sharing an author with an original paper. Independent studies find geometrically close feature families with signs of a concept hierarchy inside one dictionary (Pythia-160m, ESM-2-8M, GraphCast), but tests across SAEs of different sizes or training runs find only partial nesting, and theory says the dictionary-learning optimum cannot include a child feature that fires only with its parent.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy/theory: lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij (theory checked on toy data) limits the nesting clause within one dictionary: a child active only with its parent cannot be a dictionary-learning optimum. Per the check this is limits_scope, not a challenge, and it does not address nesting across dictionary sizes. <1B, statement as worded (families formed by splitting across sizes): R1. Nested cross-size families come only from GPT-2 small qualitative examples in lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5 and lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq. Both share authors with an original, and their split latents are picked at decoder cosine > 0.7. A group that shares no authors with an original (arXiv:2610.23801, ConSDL on CLIP ViT-B/16 and Pythia-160M, selected examples) shows only that split children lie near the parent. It does not test nesting into a concept hierarchy. <1B, families inside one dictionary: R2 for geometrically close families with hierarchy correlates (Pythia-160m, ESM-2-8M), from studies with no shared-author flag; the nesting clause is limited. The ESM-2-8M and CLIP placements follow the model names; counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size has <1B 3 and not stated 7. 1-10B: no supporting verdict; one study (Gemma 2 2B, Qwen3 4B) is limits_scope, with partial nesting of post-hoc parent-child pairs across independently trained SAEs. 10-100B and >100B: untested (counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size has no such bucket). Size not stated: GraphCast (supports, within one dictionary at a fixed width of 4,096). The original one-layer transformer is the baseline, not a test.
suggested_status.reason: Baseline (original source; described, no verdict by rule): Towards Monosemanticity shows qualitative decoder clusters of split families (base64, Arabic script) in a one-layer transformer. It says the refinement of the math/physics 'the' family is more complex than a tree, with features that split and merge. Other studies report geometrically close families with hierarchical structure on other model families. arXiv:2609.29551 (Pythia-160m, public TopK SAE) correlates the parent-child decoder gap with the theory's predicted ordering across WordNet families (partial Spearman rho, family size controlled). On a frozen holdout it gets -0.605 (L6, 75 families) and -0.914 (L11, 41 families), with randomized-sibling null p = 0.002 (500 draws). arXiv:2412.12101 (ESM-2-8M) finds a TBDR cluster with a specific detector (f/1503, F1 .998) and two broader beta-barrel features (F1 .793, .611). arXiv:2610.07583 (GraphCast, Matryoshka SAE) finds child 3153 with containment 0.953 in parent 99. arXiv:2610.23801 (ConSDL) finds CLIP ViT-B/16 children at cosine 0.65-0.75 to the parent. Limits: arXiv:2602.11881 finds partial nesting for post-hoc pairs across independently trained SAEs (baseline P(parent active | child active) 0.309-0.729, Gemma 2 2B and Qwen3 4B). In arXiv:2408.00657, direct and chained cross-size match sets have roughly bimodal overlap: apart from perfect-overlap triplets, it mostly falls at 0-0.6. lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij argues that a child active only with its parent cannot be a dictionary-learning optimum, and that hierarchies become mutually exclusive features. This qualifies 'nested' within one dictionary but does not show the families absent. Split features versus families inside one dictionary: the quantitative supports (arXiv:2609.29551, arXiv:2412.12101, arXiv:2610.07583) measure families inside one dictionary. The untested-parts lines of arXiv:2609.29551 and arXiv:2412.12101 name whether the families arise from splitting. The problems line of arXiv:2610.07583 says it does not test a range of dictionary sizes. Across sizes, arXiv:2610.23801 gives selected 4x-to-16x examples and does not test nesting into a concept hierarchy. Nested cross-size families with a shared parent appear only in GPT-2 small qualitative examples. In lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5, the six listed children of latent 8326 all carry its meta-latent 589. In lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq, families are connected at decoder cosine > 0.7, and an author comment places the weekday feature near the mean of its single-day children. Besides arXiv:2610.23801, the other independent cross-size tests, arXiv:2602.11881 and arXiv:2408.00657, are limits_scope. Author overlap: packs/studies_index.txt marks SAME GROUP on lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5 and lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq and on no other V3 study (counts: versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 2). Both are by Bart Bussmann. His name is in the author list of arXiv:2502.04878, one of the originals. The author list file gives no authors for Towards Monosemanticity, V3's linked original. By rule both posts count as the original group's extension (R1 evidence), not as independent. arXiv:2609.29551, arXiv:2412.12101, arXiv:2610.07583 and arXiv:2610.23801 carry no flag. So the statement as worded ('split features form...') is R1, and R2 holds only for families inside one dictionary. Iris decides which wording the level applies to. counts: counts.json was not rebuilt after the checks, so these V3 keys are stale. versions.V3.verdicts.challenges.studies 1 and versions.V3.studies_with_challenges 1 are lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij's verdict. The check reads it as limits_scope, so V3 has no challenges verdict, and the level rests on none. versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies 7 and limits_scope.studies 6 include the original's own supports and limits_scope lines, which should be none by rule. With those fixes applied, the V3 supports verdicts are on arXiv:2609.29551, arXiv:2412.12101, arXiv:2610.07583, arXiv:2610.23801, lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5 and lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq. The limits_scope verdicts are on arXiv:2602.11881, arXiv:2609.29551, arXiv:2605.07922, arXiv:2408.00657, arXiv:2412.12101 and lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij. versions.V3.tested_by_review_class has no 'reviewed' entry. versions.V3.main_rows_by_operation has only measurement and scaling.
suggested_status.open_questions: These results would bear on the level: (1) a quantitative test, above 1B, that families formed by splitting across dictionary sizes match an external concept hierarchy against a null; (2) a replication of the arXiv:2609.29551 decoder-gap result on another model family or SAE release; (3) parent co-firing rates in standard SAEs compared with the theory's within-dictionary prediction, and a test of nesting across sizes, which lw:jYomRhKiffA6Jnrij does not address; (4) any intervention showing the model uses the hierarchy. For the statement as worded, a test like (1) at any size, by a group that shares no authors with an original, would support R2. If Iris rewords V3 to families inside one dictionary, the R2 given for those families applies. The shared-author flag on lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5 and lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq rests on a name in arXiv:2502.04878's author list. If only V3's own linked original (Towards Monosemanticity) counts for V3, these posts become another group's qualitative cross-size examples, with closeness set by the 0.7 cosine threshold. Iris would then weigh them as such. A failed holdout replication, or evidence that the hierarchy comes from the SAE objective, would point toward C.

original_result.setup: They mapped decoder directions from three dictionaries of a one-layer transformer with UMAP and traced math and physics features across runs of increasing size.
original_result.result: Decoder directions formed clusters, such as base64 and Arabic script, with small angles between similar features. A coarse feature for 'the' in mathematical prose refined into finer ones such as machine learning and abstract algebra, but features may merge as well as split, so the structure is more complex than a tree.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: A GraphCast child feature sat nested inside its atmospheric-river parent and fired on stronger events.
Pythia-160m SAE parent–child decoder gaps correlated strongly beyond sibling nulls, including WordNet holdout.
A meta-SAE decomposed seven GPT-2-small 'talk' children's decoders into the parent's component plus more specific ones.
GPT-2 small features formed geometrically close families across SAE widths, like weekday and single-day features.
Nearby ESM-2-8M SAE features ranged from a narrow TBDR (beta-barrel subtype) detector to broader beta-barrel detectors.
In ConSDL sparse coding, child dictionary atoms lay near their parent atom, but nesting was untested.

sources.headline: Split base64 and Arabic-script features clustered tightly across dictionary sizes in a one-layer model.
Direct and step-by-step feature matches across SAE sizes overlapped only partly, so families weren't cleanly nested.
Other measures or layers weakened the hierarchy signal in parent–child decoder-vector gaps; layer 3 showed none.
Some GPT2-small SAE child features whose activations largely overlapped their parent's had unrelated meanings.
Parent–child families linked across independently trained Gemma 2 2B and Qwen3 4B SAEs nested only partially.
Kinase and glycosyltransferase feature clusters held mainly sibling specializations, with no clear general/specific hierarchy.

wording_issues.issue: Nesting is partial where it is measured. Independently trained JumpReLU SAEs with families assigned post hoc (the HSAE paper's baseline, not HSAE itself): P(parent active | child active) is 0.309–0.729 (Qwen3 4B layer 18 to Gemma 2 2B layer 20); the verdict reads the parent as a loose logical OR of its children. Top-k SAEs on text embeddings (Fig. 18b): the set overlap between direct SAE16→SAE64 and chained SAE16→SAE32→SAE64 nearest-neighbour matches is roughly bimodal; apart from perfect-overlap triplets, it generally ranges 0–0.6. The authors say clean splitting geometry would give consistent sets (r7). Theory (vanilla dictionary learning; checked on toy data, with very limited real-SAE experiments): within one dictionary, a child active only when its parent is active cannot coexist with the parent at an optimum (empty convex hull), and the hierarchy is turned into mutually exclusive features (R2). This qualifies within-dictionary nesting; the theory does not address nesting across dictionary sizes and does not show families absent.

The studies with the strongest hierarchy evidence measure families inside a single dictionary, not families formed by splitting as size grows: Pythia-160m WordNet families, ESM-2-8M clusters with no size comparison, GraphCast at a fixed width of 4,096. The untested-parts lines of arXiv:2609.29551 and arXiv:2412.12101 name whether the families arise from splitting; the problems line of arXiv:2610.07583 says it does not test a range of dictionary sizes.

Several studies do not measure closeness independently. GraphCast does not measure decoder proximity. The GPT-2 cross-size families are defined by decoder cosine > 0.7, so closeness holds by construction (verdict fix on r10). The original (baseline, described not judged) links coarse and fine features by masked cosine similarity of feature activations, not decoder geometry (R4). arXiv:2408.00657 reports no meaningful block-diagonal structure or clustering in the decoder matrix (not in rows).

wording_issues.issue: Activation-coverage children can have unrelated meaning, e.g. political tokens under a time feature (GPT2-small, case-study figures). In the ESM-2-8M layer-4 SAE, the kinase cluster's three close features are similar kinase subtypes that peak on different binding-site regions, each >0.8 on the others' max-activating examples: sibling specializations with no general/specific level (R4). The glycosyltransferase cluster (2244, 6262, 9047) does not fit this issue: the authors state 6262 is more selective, while the other two activate on all examples at nearby but different locations, a qualitative general/specific asymmetry on max-activating examples only (R5). The quantitative match to an external hierarchy (WordNet) comes from one study on Pythia-160m and depends on layer and statistic (holdout sibling-null p = 0.108 for the nonprimary L11 mean gap, r10).

All V3 rows measure SAE latents; none intervene on the model (counts: versions.V3.main_rows_by_operation has measurement 28 and scaling 3). The theory frames splitting and absorption as the objective converting a hierarchy into mutually exclusive features. The HSAE paper's problems line says its hierarchy is encouraged by its training objective.

Whether cross-size relations form a tree is unsettled. The original (baseline, described not judged) traces the math/physics 'the' features from the 512-feature run by masked activation cosine (threshold about 0.4) and says the refinement is more complex than a tree, with features that both split and merge (R4). The meta-SAE post's authors leave open whether the relations are a hierarchy or a cyclic graph (its untested-parts line; GPT-2 small layer 8). The Matryoshka post's cross-width latent trees (TinyStories model, layer 3 residual stream) are often non-tree DAGs (r9; cannot_determine: the verdict says this describes a visualization method, not a result).

method_sensitivity.what: Pythia-160m: the hierarchy is recovered with the L6 family-mean statistic (holdout −0.605) and the L11 centered-PC1 statistic (holdout −0.914). The nonprimary L11 mean-gap statistic falls inside the sibling null (p = 0.108). The text says the signal is weaker at L9 and not formed at L3.

method_sensitivity.factor: Target L0, layer and model for independently trained SAEs
method_sensitivity.what: Baseline P(parent active | child active), Gemma 2 2B layer 13: 0.662 at target L0 50, 0.634 at L0 80 and 0.619 at L0 100, with Hamming 36.1 at L0 50, 61.9 at L0 80 and 78.9 at L0 100. Layer 20 gives 0.729 and Qwen3 4B layer 18 gives 0.309. The paper also reports that constraint weight and perturbation rate trade hierarchy alignment against variance explained (HSAE only).

GPT2-small. Four MCS variants (binary or not, scaling or not) were compared on Tree SAEs only, across all L0 levels (Appendix G, Fig 20). Non-scaling-binary gave the best hierarchy metric and scaling-correlation the worst. Non-scaling-binary was then used for all MCS runs. Separately, hierarchy-metric results are reported across L0 (Fig 4) and across dictionary size (Fig 5, Tree vs Matryoshka only). All of these are figure-only, with no numbers in rows.

The one-to-many pattern is more frequent for ConSDL than for ReLU and TopK in the reported size comparisons (4× and 16×). For text-embedding SAEs, nearest-neighbour similarity decreases as k and n increase, recurrence is more common at lower k, and family activation-similarity ratios differ by dataset and SAE capacity.

GPT-2 small. The meta-SAE post (lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5) says relationships found with meta-SAEs differ from those found by comparing with smaller SAEs. Its meta-latent and SAE-3072 cosine graphs share 28.92% at matched edge counts (r3; the text calls this shared vertices in one place and shared edges in another). That post identifies split latents at decoder cosine > 0.7. It runs no sensitivity test and does not call the threshold arbitrary. The stitching post (lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq) links 768- and 1,536-latent SAEs at decoder cosine > 0.7 and states the threshold is arbitrary. It does not quantify the threshold's effect. Baseline (original; described, not judged): the original links its 'the' family across runs by masked activation cosine of about 0.4, chosen to keep the graph readable (footnote 32). This threshold is also stated as arbitrary, and its effect is not quantified.

status_amendment.public_note: The suggested level for this version drops from R2 to R1. Independent groups find hierarchy-like feature families inside a single dictionary, but nested families formed by splitting as the dictionary grows appear only in qualitative examples by an author of one of the original papers.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: R2 -> R1 for the statement as worded ('split features form nested ... families that mirror a hierarchy'). The R2 rested on quantitative supports that measure families inside one dictionary: arXiv:2609.29551 (Pythia-160m), arXiv:2412.12101 (ESM-2-8M) and arXiv:2610.07583 (GraphCast, fixed width 4,096). By their own untested-parts and problems lines, none of them tests families formed by splitting across sizes. Across sizes, nested families with a shared parent appear only in GPT-2 small qualitative examples from lw:TMAmHh4DdMr4nCSr5 and lw:baJyjpktzmcmRfosq. The studies index and author list mark both as sharing authors with an original, so they count as R1 evidence, never as independent. The independent cross-size study arXiv:2610.23801 shows only that split children lie near the parent and does not test a concept hierarchy. The other independent cross-size studies (arXiv:2602.11881, arXiv:2408.00657) give limits. R2 still fits families inside one dictionary. Whether V3 is reworded to that scope is Iris's decision.
